lines.raw: If the SSF wanted to know how many contributors have diabetes, it would face the same task: thousands of diagnosis entries have to be grouped into a few clear conditions first.
lines.say: If the S S F wanted to know how many contributors have diabetes, it would face the same task: thousands of diagnosis entries have to be grouped into a few clear conditions first.

lines.raw: The idea in one sentence.
lines.say: The idea in one sentence.

lines.raw: Condition groupers sort tens of thousands of diagnosis codes into a few hundred **clinical categories**, and chronic condition rules turn those codes into a simple **yes/no flag per member** such as "has diabetes".
lines.say: Condition groupers sort tens of thousands of diagnosis codes into a few hundred clinical categories, and chronic condition rules turn those codes into a simple yes/no flag per member such as "has diabetes".

lines.raw: The US version: CCSR.
lines.say: The U S version: C C S R.

lines.raw: In the US: Clinical Classifications Software Refined (CCSR).
lines.say: In the U S: Clinical Classifications Software Refined (C C S R).

lines.raw: Free software from **AHRQ (Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality)**, part of its HCUP (Healthcare Cost and Utilization Project) tools.
lines.say: Free software from A H R Q (Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality), part of its H C U P (Healthcare Cost and Utilization Project) tools.

lines.raw: Maps every **ICD-10-CM** diagnosis code to one or more of **more than 500 clinical categories**, organised into body systems.
lines.say: Maps every I C D 10-CM diagnosis code to one or more of more than 500 clinical categories, organised into body systems.

lines.raw: Each category has a code made of a body-system prefix and a number, for example `END002` (END = endocrine) or `CIR007` (CIR = circulatory).
lines.say: Each category has a code made of a body-system prefix and a number, for example E N D 0 0 2 (E N D = endocrine) or C I R 0 0 7 (C I R = circulatory).

lines.raw: A code that describes two problems maps to **both** categories.
lines.say: A code that describes two problems maps to both categories.

lines.raw: For example, type 2 diabetes **with** chronic kidney disease maps to "diabetes with complication" **and** to a chronic kidney disease category.
lines.say: For example, type 2 diabetes with chronic kidney disease maps to "diabetes with complication" and to a chronic kidney disease category.

lines.raw: For counting each stay **once**, CCSR also gives a **default category** for the principal diagnosis.
lines.say: For counting each stay once, C C S R also gives a default category for the principal diagnosis.

lines.raw: There is a separate CCSR for ICD-10-PCS hospital procedures.
lines.say: There is a separate C C S R for I C D 10-PCS hospital procedures.

lines.raw: Both are updated every year with the new codes.
lines.say: Both are updated every year with the new codes.

lines.raw: Example diagnosis codes and their CCSR categories (check the current CCSR release for exact assignments).
lines.say: Example diagnosis codes and their C C S R categories (check the current C C S R release for exact assignments).

lines.raw: `E11.9`. Meaning: Type 2 diabetes without complications. CCSR category: `END002` Diabetes mellitus without complication.
lines.say: E 1 1 . 9. Meaning: Type 2 diabetes without complications. C C S R category: E N D 0 0 2 Diabetes mellitus without complication.

lines.raw: `I10`. Meaning: High blood pressure (essential hypertension). CCSR category: `CIR007` Essential hypertension.
lines.say: I10. Meaning: High blood pressure (essential hypertension). C C S R category: C I R 0 0 7 Essential hypertension.

lines.raw: `M17.11`. Meaning: Primary osteoarthritis (wear-and-tear arthritis), right knee. CCSR category: `MUS006` Osteoarthritis.
lines.say: M 1 7 . 1 1. Meaning: Primary osteoarthritis (wear-and-tear arthritis), right knee. C C S R category: M U S 0 0 6 Osteoarthritis.

lines.raw: `K35.80`. Meaning: Acute appendicitis. CCSR category: A digestive-system (`DIG`) category for appendicitis.
lines.say: K 3 5 . 8 0. Meaning: Acute appendicitis. C C S R category: A digestive-system (D I G) category for appendicitis.

lines.raw: Chronic condition flags.
lines.say: Chronic condition flags.

lines.raw: A category describes a **code**.
lines.say: A category describes a code.

lines.raw: Analysts usually need a statement about a **member**: "Robert has diabetes." A **chronic condition flag** is a rule that decides this from a member's claims over a period.
lines.say: Analysts usually need a statement about a member: "Robert has diabetes." A chronic condition flag is a rule that decides this from a member's claims over a period.

lines.raw: Chronic condition.
lines.say: Chronic condition.

lines.raw: A long-lasting illness, such as diabetes, high blood pressure, asthma or heart failure.
lines.say: A long-lasting illness, such as diabetes, high blood pressure, asthma or heart failure.

lines.raw: Look-back period.
lines.say: Look-back period.

lines.raw: How far back the rule searches claims, for example 1 or 2 years.
lines.say: How far back the rule searches claims, for example 1 or 2 years.

lines.raw: Qualifying claim.
lines.say: Qualifying claim.

lines.raw: A claim with a diagnosis on the condition's code list, from an allowed claim type.
lines.say: A claim with a diagnosis on the condition's code list, from an allowed claim type.

lines.raw: Rule-out diagnosis.
lines.say: Rule-out diagnosis.

lines.raw: A code on a test ordered to **check** for a condition the patient may not have.
lines.say: A code on a test ordered to check for a condition the patient may not have.

lines.raw: Requiring two outpatient claims protects against flagging members on one test alone.
lines.say: Requiring two outpatient claims protects against flagging members on one test alone.

lines.raw: CCW.
lines.say: C C W.

lines.raw: CMS's Chronic Conditions Data Warehouse, which publishes standard chronic condition rules for Medicare data.
lines.say: CMS's Chronic Conditions Data Warehouse, which publishes standard chronic condition rules for Medicare data.

lines.raw: A typical chronic condition rule (the CCW diabetes rule, simplified).
lines.say: A typical chronic condition rule (the C C W diabetes rule, simplified).

lines.raw: Flag equals YES if, in a 2-year look-back, the member has ≥ 1 inpatient, skilled nursing or home health claim, OR ≥ 2 outpatient or doctor claims, with a diabetes code.
lines.say: Flag equals Y E S if, in a 2-year look-back, the member has ≥ 1 inpatient, skilled nursing or home health claim, O R ≥ 2 outpatient or doctor claims, with a diabetes code.

lines.raw: For example: Two outpatient claims are required because a single one could be a test to rule diabetes out.
lines.say: For example: Two outpatient claims are required because a single one could be a test to rule diabetes out.

lines.raw: Comorbidity indexes: one score from many conditions.
lines.say: Comorbidity indexes: one score from many conditions.

lines.raw: **Charlson Comorbidity Index**. What it does: Gives points for a short list of serious conditions (such as heart failure, cancer, kidney disease) and adds them up. Typical use: Adjusting outcome comparisons (for example death rates) for how ill patients were.
lines.say: Charlson Comorbidity Index. What it does: Gives points for a short list of serious conditions (such as heart failure, cancer, kidney disease) and adds them up. Typical use: Adjusting outcome comparisons (for example death rates) for how ill patients were.

lines.raw: **Elixhauser comorbidity measures**. What it does: Flags a longer list of conditions, each as yes/no; AHRQ publishes a refined version. Typical use: Research and risk adjustment of hospital outcomes.
lines.say: Elixhauser comorbidity measures. What it does: Flags a longer list of conditions, each as yes/no; A H R Q publishes a refined version. Typical use: Research and risk adjustment of hospital outcomes.

lines.raw: HCCs are a different tool.
lines.say: H C C's are a different tool.

lines.raw: HCCs also group diagnoses, but they are built to **predict cost** for risk adjustment, with hierarchies and payment weights.
lines.say: H C C's also group diagnoses, but they are built to predict cost for risk adjustment, with hierarchies and payment weights.

lines.raw: They are taught in the Risk Adjustment course.
lines.say: They are taught in the Risk Adjustment course.

lines.say: Why it matters for data.

lines.raw: Decide whether your question is about **codes**, **claims** or **members**.
lines.say: Decide whether your question is about codes, claims or members.

lines.raw: Counting CCSR categories across all claims counts **visits** for diabetes; counting members with a diabetes flag counts **people** with diabetes.
lines.say: Counting C C S R categories across all claims counts visits for diabetes; counting members with a diabetes flag counts people with diabetes.

lines.raw: And because one code can map to several CCSR categories, adding categories together can count the same claim twice: use the default category when every claim must be counted once.
lines.say: And because one code can map to several C C S R categories, adding categories together can count the same claim twice: use the default category when every claim must be counted once.

lines.raw: Key takeaways.
lines.say: Key takeaways.

lines.raw: CCSR (from AHRQ) groups ICD-10-CM codes into more than 500 clinical categories by body system.
lines.say: C C S R (from A H R Q) groups I C D 10-CM codes into more than 500 clinical categories by body system.

lines.raw: One diagnosis code can map to more than one category; the default category counts each stay once.
lines.say: One diagnosis code can map to more than one category; the default category counts each stay once.

lines.raw: Chronic condition flags turn claims into a yes/no per member, using a look-back period and a claim-count rule.
lines.say: Chronic condition flags turn claims into a yes/no per member, using a look-back period and a claim-count rule.

lines.raw: Comorbidity indexes (Charlson, Elixhauser) summarise many conditions into one score or set of flags.
lines.say: Comorbidity indexes (Charlson, Elixhauser) summarise many conditions into one score or set of flags.
